exemplars.title: Designing Human-AI Collaboration to Support Learning in Counterspeech Writing
exemplars.why: The user commits selections before the system evaluates them, and the interface then computes correctness and provides a side-by-side view that makes differences in interpretation directly inspectable.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 2711 because it explicitly computes and displays the human-system discrepancy, whereas rid 2711 leaves disagreement implicit in the interaction sequence.

exemplars.title: Are You Really Sure? Understanding the Effects of Human Self-Confidence Calibration in AI-Assisted Decision Making
exemplars.why: It provides an especially clean commit-reveal-redecide sequence: the user records an initial judgment and confidence, receives the AI recommendation and potentially its confidence, and then makes a final judgment.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 10282 because its parallel treatment of human and AI confidence makes the paired assessments more legible, while still retaining the complete revision sequence.

exemplars.title: Adjust for Trust: Mitigating Trust-Induced Inappropriate Reliance on AI Assistance
exemplars.why: The interface preserves an independent human decision, reveals AI advice for the same problem, solicits a revised decision, and then connects observed accuracy to an explicit trust update.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 9169 because it establishes commitment, AI reveal, and revision, whereas rid 9169 only establishes review of self-reported and system-generated scores.

notes: The selected membership matches the consensus top three, but the order does not: rid 14026 moves ahead of rid 10282 because it is the only candidate whose evidence explicitly says the system compares the assessments and offers a side-by-side difference view. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should distrust any inference that these examples fully satisfy every clause of the structural signature: rid 14026 does not explicitly document a revision affordance, and its “system-defined reference answer” may be fixed rather than model-generated; rid 2711 and rid 10282 document temporal commit-reveal-revise sequences but do not establish that both verdicts remain visible together or that their difference is explicitly rendered or computed.
